title: Build: async job / notification pipeline
summary: Broker, workers and a fake vendor as separate processes on localhost: a durable leased queue, retries with backoff + jitter, idempotency at both ends, dead letters and replay, backpressure and graceful drain, all proven by failure injection.

units.title: A durable queue and a pool of workers
Retries and idempotency at the vendor boundary
Dead letters, backpressure, drain and the failure run

labs.title: Job pipeline as three processes: broker (checksummed log, leases, nack delays, producer keys, DLQ and replay, depth bound), worker (bounded pool, classification, backoff + jitter, stable idempotency key, drain) and a fake vendor; milestone and failure-injection tests

outcomes.text: Implement a durable job broker on an append-only, checksummed log that survives SIGKILL and a torn tail, and explain which writes must be fsynced before acknowledging and which may not be.
Implement leases with visibility timeouts and per-attempt lease tokens, and explain why that makes delivery at-least-once and what a lease expiry means for a job that is still running.
Build a worker pool with bounded concurrency and long-polling that survives a broker outage or partition without exiting, spinning or overloading the vendor.
Classify vendor responses (timeout, 429, 5xx, other 4xx) into retryable and permanent, and implement exponential backoff with full or equal jitter and Retry-After as a floor, without overflow.
Make the pipeline effectively exactly-once at the vendor with a producer idempotency key at the broker and a stable consumer key per job, and show with a SIGKILL between effect and ack that it holds.
Dead-letter permanent failures, exhausted retries and jobs that keep killing workers with their attempt history, keep a poison job from blocking the queue, and replay safely after a fix.
Apply backpressure with a depth bound that answers 429 + Retry-After (and still recognises a producer's retry), and size the bound from drain time and memory.
Drain a worker on SIGTERM without losing or duplicating work, with a bounded drain time, and relate it to an orchestrator's grace period.
Write a design rationale that predicts the behaviour of every failure-injection scenario, then compare it with what the processes did and explain every difference.
Compact the log, add a shared retry budget across workers, and place the producer's transactional outbox and a partitioned broker in the design.
